Zone outlines

Transcribed, not verified. Rates were read from the scanned book by eye. Rows marked “uncertain” had a digit inferred from the clipped scan. Check against the book, then mark verified.

How a zone is decided

The map layers are scans of the printed “sketch plan, not to scale” ward and zone maps. They contain no zone boundaries as data. Someone has to trace each zone on the Zones tab and approve it. A lookup only uses outlines that are approved, on a map whose placement is approved.

Verified match
Inside exactly one zone and more than 5 m from its edge.
Boundary review
On, or within 5 m of, an edge. No zone is chosen. Review by hand.
Ambiguous
Inside overlapping outlines of different zones. No zone is chosen.
No zone found
No approved outline contains the point.
Geometry not verified
Only draft outlines exist near the point. They are never matched.
Distances are in metres on a local flat projection of the map. A match shows only that the point lies inside a traced outline. It does not prove ownership, the accuracy of the sketch, or a parcel boundary.
Map placement comes from a box drawn by eye in Google Earth, so its accuracy is unmeasured. Approving it records that you accept it as approximate.

Valuation

Estimated base amount = rate per sq. m × area in sq. m. Square feet are converted with 1 sq ft = 0.09290304 m². Rates only apply inside their effective period (calendar year 2001). No adjustments are applied. This is not a market value or a certified valuation.

Not in this page

Address search needs a geocoding service that a hosted page cannot reach, so use coordinates or a full Google Maps link. The full application with a Python/PostGIS backend is a separate download.
